perspective:
From Jose Castillo’s perspective:

- I work with Patricia at the community bank and occasionally help with maintenance and repairs there.
- I noticed she seemed more withdrawn and less vibrant than usual during our shifts, so I asked if she was okay.
- She told me it was “nothing really,” just some personal stuff, and thanked me for asking.
- I offered to listen if she ever wanted to talk, and she said she appreciated that.
- During a lunch break, I overheard her on the phone sounding worried about bills and financial commitments.
- I told her managing finances can be stressful and mentioned I’d been reading up on financial planning strategies.
- She said that could be helpful and that she’d been overwhelmed with her bills lately.
- I suggested we could look over budgeting tips together, and she said she’d take me up on it soon.
- Afterward, I worried I might have overstepped by bringing up money, so I clarified I only wanted to help, not pry.
- She told me she didn’t think I was prying and was actually grateful I offered.
- I said I respected her privacy and wanted to support her as a friend, and she said she really appreciated that.
- Later, I checked in with her by asking about weekend plans. She said she was doing all good and planned a quiet weekend at home.
- I told her she could find me if she ever needed anything or wanted to chat, and she thanked me.
- At another point I offered to help with anything, even just getting coffee. She said she was busy but handling it, thanked me for checking in, and said it was great to have my support.
- I responded that she was welcome anytime and that we’re all there to help each other out.
